title: Consensus learning nominates a pulmonary-hypertension miRNA pattern
summary: Four fitted feature-selection approaches consistently selected miR-636 and miR-187-5p in a pulmonary arterial hypertension study. The clinical miRNA models showed moderate discrimination in a small held-out subset. These are exploratory diagnostic-reference and feature-association findings, not established clinical utility or causal pulmonary mechanisms.
ai_technology: Boruta random forest; LASSO; regression partition trees; XGBoost
organization: University of Sheffield; Imperial College London

source_review.scope: Exact primary front and selected computational/clinical Methods and corresponding high-level Results; operational laboratory protocols excluded from review

evidence.tested: The miRNA cohort comprised 64 PAH cases and 43 combined healthy/systemic-sclerosis-without-PH controls. Models were developed using 72 people and assessed on 35; repeated cross-validation supported feature selection and tuning. Both nominated miRNAs recurred across the four approaches and alternative selection analyses.
evidence.unknown: Model and feature comparisons used the same small validation sample. The Results claim 30/35 correct for Boruta, while the table reports a different classification rate; no single accuracy is promoted here. Whole-data filtering and multiple selection analyses require caution. Whole-blood gene-target classification involved refitting on different features and is not external validation of the original miRNA classifier. A five-year follow-up does not make the already-collected diagnostic evaluation prospective. No pathway causality or laboratory mechanism is adopted.
evidence.ai_role: Learned forests, boosted trees and regularized/partition models select diagnostic features and produce patient-level predictions; agreement of selected features and held-out reference discrimination supply the scoped finding.
